stem: When Dorothy looks out from her doorway in Kansas, what does she see on every side?
choices: A great gray prairie
Tall green cornfields
A thick, dark forest
Hills covered in flowers

evidence.quote: she could see nothing but the great gray prairie on every side

explanation: Kansas is described as gray and flat, with not a tree or a house in sight. That makes the colors of Oz stand out later.

stem: What kind of shoes is the Wicked Witch of the East wearing when Dorothy's house lands on her?
choices: Silver shoes
Ruby slippers
Golden boots
Glass slippers

evidence.quote: two feet were sticking out, shod in silver shoes with pointed toes

explanation: In the book the shoes are silver. The ruby slippers come from the 1939 movie, so this one checks who read the book.

stem: "Cried Dorothy, clasping her hands together in dismay." What does dismay mean here?
choices: Worry and shock
Excitement and joy
Boredom
Sleepiness

evidence.quote: cried Dorothy, clasping her hands together in dismay. “The house must have fallen on her. Whatever shall we do?”

explanation: Dorothy has just realized her house fell on someone and asks what to do. Clasping her hands and crying out shows she is shocked and upset.

stem: What does the Good Witch of the North give Dorothy to keep her safe?
choices: A kiss on the forehead
A magic wand to carry
A golden cap to wear
A map of the yellow road

evidence.quote: She came close to Dorothy and kissed her gently on the forehead. Where her lips touched the girl they left a round, shining mark

explanation: The kiss leaves a shining mark, and no one dares hurt someone the Witch of the North has kissed.

stem: How did the Tin Woodman end up made of tin?
choices: The Wicked Witch enchanted his axe, so it kept cutting him
He fell into a river and rusted all over
The Wizard turned him to tin as a punishment
He was built by a tinsmith to guard the forest

evidence.quote: Thereupon the Wicked Witch enchanted my axe

explanation: Each time the axe cut off part of him, a tinsmith replaced it with tin, until he was tin all over.

stem: Why do Dorothy and the Lion fall asleep in the field of flowers?
choices: The smell of so many poppies makes anyone who breathes it sleep
They walked all night and were tired out
The Wicked Witch cast a sleeping spell on them
The Scarecrow sang them a lullaby

evidence.quote: their odor is so powerful that anyone who breathes it falls asleep

explanation: The poppies' smell puts people and animals to sleep. The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman are fine because they don't breathe.

stem: What does the Guardian of the Gate make everyone wear in the Emerald City?
choices: Green spectacles
Green hats
Silver shoes
Golden crowns

evidence.quote: wear spectacles the brightness and glory of the Emerald City would blind you

explanation: The Guardian says the city is so bright it would blind them, so he locks green spectacles on everyone.

stem: When Dorothy goes alone to see Oz in the throne room, what does he look like?
choices: An enormous head with no body
A beautiful lady with wings
A terrible beast
A ball of fire

evidence.quote: In the center of the chair was an enormous Head, without a body to support it or any arms or legs whatever.

explanation: Oz appears in a different shape to each visitor. To Dorothy he is a giant head; the others see a lady, a beast, and a ball of fire.

stem: What makes Dorothy throw the bucket of water on the Wicked Witch of the West?
choices: The Witch tricked her and took one of her silver shoes
The Witch was about to hurt the Lion
Glinda told her that water would melt the Witch
The Witch set the castle kitchen on fire

evidence.quote: She placed a bar of iron in the middle of the kitchen floor, and then by her magic arts made the iron invisible to human eyes.
This made Dorothy so very angry that she picked up the bucket of water that stood near and dashed it over the Witch

explanation: The Witch tripped Dorothy with an invisible iron bar and grabbed a shoe. Dorothy threw the water out of anger, not knowing it would melt her.

stem: Oz admits the Emerald City is "no more" green than any other city. Why does it look green to everyone?
choices: He made everyone wear green spectacles
It is built from real emeralds
A spell turns everything green at night
The sun in Oz shines green

evidence.quote: I put green spectacles on all the people, so that everything they saw was green

explanation: The city's magic is a trick. Like the Wizard himself, it seems wonderful only because of how people are made to see it.

stem: When the Scarecrow finds out Oz is just a common man, what does he call him?
choices: A humbug
A villain
A coward
A wizard after all

evidence.quote: “you’re a humbug.” “Exactly so!” declared the little man

explanation: A humbug is someone who fools people. Oz happily agrees that he is one.

stem: Oz fills the Scarecrow's head with bran, pins, and needles and calls them "bran-new brains." What does this suggest?
choices: He already had the cleverness; he needed to believe it
Oz really has strong magic and fixed the Scarecrow
Brains can only be found inside the Emerald City
The Scarecrow will never become clever at all

evidence.quote: Hereafter you will be a great man, for I have given you a lot of bran-new brains.

explanation: The Scarecrow had been coming up with the group's best ideas the whole trip. The bran 'brains' are a joke; what changes is his belief in himself.

stem: How do the Silver Shoes carry Dorothy home?
choices: She knocks the heels together three times and gives a command
She clicks them together while saying a magic poem aloud
She throws them high into the air when the sun rises
She walks backward three steps in them and makes a wish

evidence.quote: All you have to do is to knock the heels together three times and command the shoes to carry you wherever you wish to go.

explanation: Glinda explains that the shoes can take her anywhere in three steps once she knocks the heels together and gives the command.

stem: Put these events in the order they happen.

events.text: Dorothy helps the Scarecrow down from his pole

evidence.quote: “We will go to the Emerald City and ask the Great Oz how to get back to Kansas again.”

events.text: The Lion knocks the Scarecrow into the road

evidence.quote: With one blow of his paw he sent the Scarecrow spinning over and over to the edge of the road

events.text: Dorothy breathes in the scent of the scarlet poppies

evidence.quote: as she breathed in the spicy scent of the bright flowers

events.text: The Guardian of the Gate hands out spectacles

evidence.quote: wear spectacles the brightness and glory of the Emerald City would blind you

explanation: The trip goes: the Scarecrow, the Lion, the poppy field, and then the gate of the Emerald City.

stem: Put these events in the order they happen.

events.text: Dorothy sees Oz as a giant head

evidence.quote: In the center of the chair was an enormous Head, without a body to support it

events.text: Dorothy throws water on the Wicked Witch of the West

evidence.quote: she picked up the bucket of water that stood near and dashed it over the Witch

events.text: The Scarecrow calls Oz a humbug

evidence.quote: “you’re a humbug.” “Exactly so!” declared the little man

events.text: Dorothy is home and hugs Aunt Em

evidence.quote: “And here is Toto, too. And oh, Aunt Em! I’m so glad to be at home again!”

explanation: Dorothy meets Oz, is sent to defeat the Witch, comes back and uncovers the humbug, and finally gets home.
